digest.component_or_area: rebar CLI command parsing for positional-body commands
propositions: When rebar comment (or other positional-body commands) receives a flag-looking token like --body-file or --body as the body argument, it silently stores the flag token itself as the comment body, discards the intended content, and exits 0, defeating the ticket store's durability contract.
A body argument beginning with - must be rejected with non-zero exit and corrective message, unless preceded by -- to indicate the user intentionally meant a dash-prefixed value.

The same CLI argument-parsing guard must apply consistently across all positional-body commands (comment, create, edit, session-log, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands) rather than being repeated or forgotten per command.
An args[:min_args] slice downstream of the flag-token-as-body bug compounds the silent loss: surplus positionals holding the intended value are also discarded, so the failure is doubly quiet.

Two independent sessions have each lost substantial recorded work (root-cause analysis, fix rationale, blast-radius audit) to this footgun, discovered only when downstream gates (completion verifier) found no evidence backing the purported writes.
